references.text: Repeats the command that all men must appear before the Lord three times a year, expanding on the three festivals mentioned in verse 14.
A parallel law text commanding that all men must appear before the Lord, the God of Israel, three times a year.
Summarizes the three annual pilgrimage festivals: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Tabernacles.
A detailed description of the Lord's appointed feasts, including the three major pilgrimage festivals that Israel was to celebrate.
Prescribes the offerings to be brought during the Passover festival and the Festival of Weeks, two of the three annual feasts.
Describes the offerings for the Festival of Tabernacles, the third of the annual pilgrimage festivals.
Solomon maintained the practice of celebrating the three annual feasts: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Tabernacles.
The verse gives the divine guarantee of safety that makes it possible to fulfill the command for three pilgrimages.
